title: Payment Terms, Overdue Interest and the Credit Limit (Corporate Travel Programmes)
content:
Invoices on the Corporate Travel Programmes fall due within the tier's payment terms counted from the invoice date, and an overdue balance carries the tier's monthly interest from the day after it falls due.

A programme whose unpaid balance passes the tier's credit limit is suspended rather than allowed to book further.

Where the company elects to be invoiced in a currency other than the contract currency, the tier's conversion markup is added to each invoice.

## What the balance is

The balance on a programme is the net amount billed to the company on it. Subscriptions, seat licences, transaction fees, overage and interest credit that account, and credit notes and rebates debit it. It is that net figure, not any single invoice, that is measured against the tier's credit limit.

## The clock on an overdue balance

| Point in time | Standing of the balance |
| --- | --- |
| The invoice date | The payment terms of the tier begin to run from this date |
| Any day inside the tier's payment terms | The invoice is not yet due, and no interest arises |
| The day the payment terms expire | The invoice falls due |
| The day after the invoice falls due | Interest at the tier's monthly rate begins to run on the overdue balance |

Where a tier's payment terms are 0 days from the invoice date, the invoice falls due on the invoice date itself, and interest at that tier's monthly rate runs from the day after the invoice date.

## Notes from credit control

- The interest published for a tier is a monthly rate on the overdue balance, not a one-off charge and not a daily rate.
- The currency markup is added to each invoice, and it arises only where the company has elected to be invoiced in a currency other than the contract currency.
- Passing the credit limit is answered by suspension of the programme, not by allowing further booking on the unpaid balance.
